settings.stamp_text: CARVED BY HAND · NO TWO ALIKE
settings.heading: Carved by Hand, by Jim
settings.text:
My name's Jim. I served in the U.S. Army, and I came home without part of my leg. That's the short version — the rest I'll keep between me and the men I served with.

What I'll tell you is what came after. Recovery is long, and it leaves you with a lot of quiet hours and a need to do something with your hands. I started out in the garage with a few tools and a block of wood, trying to carve the one flag I could never find in a store — the real thing, not a picture of it printed on plastic.

The first one took me weeks. A neighbor asked for one. Then his brother. Somewhere in there it stopped being a way to pass the time and turned into the thing I do.

Every flag still leaves my shop the same way: solid wood, cut and carved and finished by hand, the stars and stripes and the eagle worked down into the grain so you can feel them under your fingers. No two come out the same, because no two pieces of wood are. I put my hands on every one before it ships — if it isn't right, it doesn't go out.

It's slow work. It's meant to be. A flag like this isn't something you replace next season. It's something you hang once and hand down. That's the whole idea.

Thank you for letting me keep doing it.
